title: Fix arm64 r-devel failure in ObliqueForest node assignment test
description:
The linux-arm64 r-devel check (https://github.com/r-devel/linux-arm64-checks/tree/HEAD/lorax) fails in `test-ObliqueForest.R` ("node assignments are consistent"): two observations swap sides of an oblique split. This is most likely a floating-point tie at the split threshold (FMA / operation order differences between aorsf's C++ and R's evaluation of the rule), not a logic bug.

Observations whose split score is within `1e-8 * max(1, abs(threshold))` of any threshold in the rule are dropped from both sides of the `expect_setequal()` comparison. No package code changes, so no NEWS bullet.

title: add S3 methods for tidymodels objects
Faster rule extraction
description:
This PR increases the speed of extracting rules. The main cause was that `extract_rules.party()` looked up each leaf's parent by looping over every node in the tree, which is quadratic or worse per tree. Several other methods had the same per-leaf `*_find_parent` pattern. Most users extract rules from every tree in an ensemble, so the work was benchmarked on that case.

## Changes

### Speedups

- **party, cforest, ranger, randomForest, grf:** `extract_rules.party()` now does one top-down walk per tree that carries the split expressions down and emits a rule at each leaf. ranger, randomForest and grf also skipped a row-by-row computation of fitted node ids (nrow × depth per tree) by passing a zero-row copy of the data.
- **rpart:** one top-down walk with a precomputed split-row lookup.
- **xgboost, lightgbm, bart, catboost:** one model dump, `getTrees()` call or JSON export now covers all requested trees. Previously it was repeated per tree, which made the total quadratic. Each tree is then converted with a top-down walk.
- **aorsf (`ObliqueForest`):** the slow R6 accessors (`get_means()`, `get_stdev()`, `get_fctr_info()`, `get_names_x()`) are cached once, and each tree is a top-down walk.
- **C5.0 and Cubist:** already fast, unchanged apart from the shared checks below.

Output is `identical()` to the old code wherever the old code could produce output.

### Timings

| Method | Before | After | Case |
|---|---|---|---|
| ranger | 115 s | 1.7 s per 20 trees | 2 small trees before, 20 trees on 2,000 rows after |
| randomForest | 422 s | 1.7 s per 20 trees | 2 small trees before, 20 trees on 2,000 rows after |
| grf | 661 s | 0.25 s | 10 trees, 1,000 rows |
| rpart | 4.1 s | 0.12 s | |
| bart | 7.6 s | 0.19 s | 100 trees × 2 chains |
| lightgbm | 6.8 s | 0.25 s | 50 trees |
| xgboost | 1.2 s | 0.19 s | 40 trees |
| catboost | 0.6–1.1 s | 0.17 s | 100 trees |
| aorsf | 1.5 s | 0.39 s | 20 trees |

The ranger and randomForest "before" and "after" rows are not the same workload, so they understate the improvement.

### Test suite timings

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test-cforest.R` | skipped (estimated 1–2 hours if enabled) | about 2 s |
| `test-party.R` | skipped (7:43 when enabled) | about 1.7 s |

Both files were slow because of model fitting, not rule extraction. `partykit::cforest()` and `ctree()` were fit on `wa_trees`, where `county` has 30 levels (one 3-tree cforest fit took about 170 s, while extraction took 0.01–0.03 s). A new test helper, `get_wa_trees_small_data()`, keeps 200 rows and the 3 most common counties and labels the rest `other`. A 3-tree fit now takes 0.02 s. The `skip()` and the random `skip_if(runif(1) <= 0.1)` are removed, and `tests/testthat/_snaps/cforest.md` is new because those snapshots were never recorded.

### API and behavior changes

- **`tree` accepts a vector** for ObliqueForest, bart, catboost, lightgbm and xgboost, matching the other ensemble methods.
- **Shared validation:** new internal `check_tree_type()` and `check_tree_range()` are used by every method with a `tree` argument (including C5.0 trials, Cubist committees, cforest and `active_predictors.cforest()`). The range error now states the upper limit, for example "`tree` must be between 1 and 3, the number of trees in the model."
- **Tree counts:** `num_ensemble_members()` is the single source for the number of trees. Internal `lgb_num_trees()`, `xgb_num_trees()` and `bart_num_trees()` take an already-read dump so the model is not dumped a second time.
- **`rlang::check_dots_empty()`** is now called first in every `extract_rules()` method, so typos such as `trees = 2` error instead of being silently ignored. As a result `data` is no longer accepted by `extract_rules.C5.0()`.
- **grf:** the fallback of 1000 trees is removed, `num_ensemble_members.grf()` aborts clearly when the number of trees is missing, and matrices without column names no longer error.

## Tests

- New test that every training row matches exactly one party rule and that the rule `id` equals `predict(type = "node")`.
- New "handles several trees in one call" tests for lightgbm, xgboost, catboost, ObliqueForest and bart.
- New tests with snapshots for `check_tree_type()` and `check_tree_range()`.
- Snapshots updated for the new error messages. The `tree = c(1, 2)` error snapshots were removed because that call is now valid. `data =` was removed from the C5.0 tests.
- Full suite: 2,545 passing, 0 failing, 1 skipped (aorsf "On Mac").

title: Catboost support
description:
`active_predictors()`, `as.party()`, `extract_rules()`, and `var_imp()` now have methods for catboost models (`catboost.Model`). 

Symmetric and non-symmetric trees are supported, as are one-hot encoded categorical splits; ~splits based on categorical target statistics (CTRs) cannot be converted to rules.~ We added support for most CTR splits. 

Relies on a non-CRAN package (catboost) 🤞

title: add as.party methods
description:
Closes #2 

A variety of conversion tools for `partykit::as.party()`. Let Claude rewrite the one that is already in C50 since that is a pretty ugly implementation.

It added methods for: `bart`, `C5.0`, `grf`, `lgb.Booster`, `randomForest`, `ranger`, `regression_forest`, and `xgb.Booster`. 

Also sets up the infrastructure for the myriad packages in Suggests.
